sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global App Store Optimization and Multilingual Organic Search

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 10 July 2020; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019 on the practical operation of the RBE; CSSF Regulation No 12-02; EU Regulation 2015/847 on transfers of funds

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and extract from the RCS of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) or equivalent foreign trade registrar

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the articles of association and current ownership structure of each corporate member
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chamber of Commerce / corporate registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of residential address for each director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consulate of Luxembourg in the person's country of residence or authorized notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (if issuing country is not a Hague Convention member; otherwise Hague Apostille)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate (Bulletin N°3) or equivalent for each proposed manager (gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Public Prosecutor's Office (Casier judiciaire) or competent national authority of the manager's country of original residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization as appropriate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP identification under EU AML/CFT standards with enhanced due diligence for family members and known associates; mandatory screening against the Luxembourg consolidated AML/CFT financial sanctions list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions database, UN Security Council consolidated list, and US OFAC SDN list. For the ASO/SEO localization agency business, the industrial sector is classified as Low_Risk_Standard, yet the notary, RBE registrar, and banking payment partners still require full customer due diligence on all shareholders, managers, and UBOs prior to incorporation and account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – My RCSL online portal (https://www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be composed of Latin script characters and may be expressed in English, French, German, or Luxembourgish. The name must be unique, non-confusing, not misleading, and must include or be accompanied by 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or an accepted abbreviation such as 'SARL' or 'S.à r.l.'. Non-Latin transliterations are not accepted; all statutory names must be reserved and registered in Latin script.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS online portal rejects the name reservation, the applicant may resubmit with a modified name or submit a decisive distinctiveness argument via the same portal. A formal administrative appeal may be addressed to the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade through the RCS Office within one month from the date of the rejection notice, and may be followed by judicial appeal before the Tribunal administratif if denial is sustained. Any name reservation may be renewed once before expiry, and the final corporate law deed must incorporate the reserved name exactly as cleared.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office of a Luxembourg SARL. The company must maintain a real statutory registered office in Luxembourg; however, professional domiciliation by a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation company is acceptable for this low-risk digital app-growth agency, provided the arrangement goes beyond letterbox status and is supported by local operational documentation, decision-making, or administrative infrastructure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% annual probability in the first year of operation for a standard Low_Risk_Standard industry; probability increases to approximately 15% if the entity applies for significant VAT refunds, has high intra-group flows, or is flagged by the CSSF or Luxembourg AML authorities for enhanced supervision.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and clearance certificate (certificat de non-confusion)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official portal fee charged by the Luxembourg Business Registers

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Approved registered office through licensed domiciliation agent (minimum one year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-volume service company domiciliation in Luxembourg

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation including notarial legalization of signatures
Filing of instrument of incorporation and coordinated statutes at the RCS
Publication of the legal notice of incorporation in the Mémorial B and RCS gazette
UBO register (RBE) filing and related AML/FICOV screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RBE (Luxembourg Business Registers) and AML compliance provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Combined official RBE handling and automated PEP/sanctions screening benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization processing for founding shareholder documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed consular fee per document plus professional courier cost; benchmark $80-120 per document for an average two-document set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of articles of association and shareholder resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Standard fixed fee for a SARL with two or fewer partners and an ordinary UBO structure

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended); SARL governed by Book I, Title IV, Articles 710-1 to 710-24, further modernised by the Law of 23 September 2020 on the modernisation of commercial companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), managed by the Ministry of Justice
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution en la forme authentique notariée (Notarial Deed of Incorporation) including the Statuts (Articles of Association), filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for a SARL is EUR 12,000. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and at least 20% paid up upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years; funds must be deposited in a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) opened with a Luxembourg credit institution or held at the Caisse de Consignation, and evidenced by a notarial bank certificate (attestation de blocage). Capital can also be formed by in-kind contributions, subject to statutory control.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] S.À R.L.

The undersigned, acting as founding managers and shareholders of the Company, resolve as follows:
1. SHARE CAPITAL: The issued share capital, as allocated in the deed of incorporation, is hereby approved and the bank confirmation of the escrow deposit is acknowledged. The legal reserve requirement is accepted.
2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company is fixed at [ADDRESS], Luxembourg. The file of publications and correspondence is placed at this address, subject to relocation by simple resolution.
3. OFFICERS: [NAME] is appointed as manager (Gérant), with full powers and sole signature authority to bind the Company.
4. EFFECTIVENESS: This resolution takes effect upon signing.

Adopted on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online pre-check portal at lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search in the RCS central index; confirm that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing trade names and that the legal form suffix 'S.à r.l.' is appended; submit a written reservation request, valid for up to two months, stating the company form, registered office address and the intended corporate object, via the electronic filing interface MyGuichet.lu or directly to LBR.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and statutory suffix
Identification documents of each founding shareholder
CV and identification of the proposed manager (Gérant)
Draft corporate object (ISIC 7310 digital marketing services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused on grounds of confusing similarity, file a fresh alternative name application featuring a distinct distinctive element; a final refusal can be contested before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of the Articles of Association (Statuts) and Notarial Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Notaire) acting under the authority of the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary with the reserved corporate name, corporate object, share capital structure, managerial power scheme and registered office details; review and validate the draft statuts to ensure mandatory SARL clauses under Article 710-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915 are included, including valuation of any in-kind contributions and restrictions on share transfers.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Passport copies of shareholders and managers
Proof of residential address for all individuals
Business plan and bank reference
Beneficial owner questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises legal objections to a clause, instruct amendments by supplemental note; if the parties dispute valuation of in-kind contributions, obtain an independent auditor's report or adjust the deed to avoid nullity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Escrow Capital Account and Deposit of Paid-up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) or the Caisse de Consignation (State Consignment Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account (compte bloqué) in the name of the company 'in formation', deposit at minimum EUR 12,000 nominal capital with at least 20% paid up on account; instruct the bank to issue a notarial capital confirmation certificate (attestation de blocage) certifying that the funds are held to the order of the company and irrevocably reserved for its formation.
required_dossiers: Pre-incorporation draft statuts
Identity documents of the deposit holder
Source of funds declaration and bank references
AML/KYC forms of the credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence, provide corroborative source-of-wealth evidence such as tax returns or asset management statements; if the account is refused, apply to the Caisse de Consignation as a statutory alternative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the signing session of all founders and appointed managers; verify everyone's identity and legal capacity; sign the deed of incorporation incorporating the statuts, capital subscription lists, appointment of managers and address of registered office; the notary is responsible for submitting the deed and extracts to the RCS and arranging publication.
required_dossiers: Final approved statuts
Bank capital blocking certificate (attestation de blocage)
Minutes of the founding shareholder decision
Consent of the appointed manager(s)
Notarized powers of attorney for remote founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a founder is absent, execute a notarized power of attorney or postpone the deed without extinguishing subscription; if a signature defect is discovered, sign a corrective rectification deed (acte rectificatif).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed and its legalised extracts electronically through the RCS e-filing interface after the notary's transmission; pay the registration duty and publication tariff for the RESA official gazette; upon admission, obtain the RCS registration number, the RCS extract and the legal entity identifier registration.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation
Bank capital certificate (already transmitted by notary)
Appointment acceptances signed by managers
Beneficial owner declaration (RBE) filed concurrently
Foreign registration certificate for foreign managers if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an incompleteness query (défaut de pièces), supply the missing documents within the prescribed legal period; if a formal refusal occurs, instruct the notary to execute a rectification deed and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and VAT Number Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED), via MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate income tax and municipal business tax registration file to the competent local tax office (bureau d'imposition) for the district of the registered office; apply for the Luxembourg VAT number (TVA) electronically within 15 days of incorporation; open the electronic tax mailbox and confirm the annual accounting period.
required_dossiers: Recent RCS extract
Statuts and notarial deed
Identity documents of legal manager(s)
Proof of registered office address
Powers of attorney for tax representatives if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax file is deemed incomplete, attend the local bureau d'imposition with supplementary documents; for VAT, file a corrective electronic application and escalate to the AED helpdesk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Owner Register Filing and Establishment Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE register) and Ministry of the Economy via the Guichet unique (Guichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial owners with the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) within one month of RCS registration; complete the declaration of establishment (déclaration d'établissement) for the non-regulated commercial service activity corresponding to ISIC 7310, verifying that no prior ministerial authorisation is required for the activity, and obtain a proof of declaration.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Beneficial owner information and ownership chains
Identities of ultimate natural persons controlling the SARL
Address of the establishment
Rental agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE filing is rejected due to unclear control structures, file a corporate organisational chart and share register excerpts; if the establishment declaration is queried, provide the ISIC activity classification and statutory exemption reference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security Registration and Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) and Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the CCSS to obtain the employer number and affiliation for occupational insurance; secure occupational safety clearance of the registered office by verifying that the premises meet fire safety and workplace ergonomics standards; retain the ITM inspection reference for payroll and health and safety compliance.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Identification of officers
Rental contract (bail commercial) of registered office
List of future employees and work schedules
Fire safety documentation for the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS registration is delayed, present the RCS extract and signed employment intentions; if the ITM flags safety deficiencies, perform corrective works and submit a compliance report to reopen the file.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des PME et de l'entrepreneuriat, exercising commercial professions control through the Guichet unique (Guichet.lu)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aucune autorisation d'établissement préalable requise (No prior establishment licence required for non-regulated services under ISIC 7310); only an annual declaration of commercial activity is filed via Guichet.lu

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Administration), under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Registration not required: office-based marketing and localization services are not listed among activities subject to an EIA or environmental permit under the Law of 31 May 1999; no OPARL/SEVESO classification
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for any industrial discharge; general municipal wastewater and waste ordinances apply, e-waste handling must comply with the transposed Directive 2012/19/EU on waste electrical and electronic equipment, and office energy consumption must meet general building efficiency norms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificat de sécurité incendie) by the communal fire prevention service under the Law of 28 December 2006; workplace occupational clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) under the Law of 17 June 1994 on safety and health at work; structural load inspection is not required for ordinary office premises but the lessor must certify the premises are compliant with the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on access to professions for commercial premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and indirect taxes. Official e-portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://myguichet.lu) and guichet.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL), incorporation before a Luxembourg notary is first filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL), which issues the national identification number (matricule). A VAT identification number (TVA LUXXXXXXXX) is obtained separately by submitting the electronic registration form (Form 010) to the AEDT via MyGuichet, supported by notarized articles of association, RCSL registration certificate, proof of registered office and effective management place in Luxembourg, and identification documents of managers. The corporate income tax TIN is aligned with the RCSL matricule; no additional direct-tax registration is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident SARL is subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (IBT) and net wealth tax (NWT) on worldwide profits, with tax credits/exemptions for certain foreign-source income. No US-style pass-through eligibility; no tax-exempt zone applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box election. Available statutory elections include (i) tax consolidation (fiscal unity) under Section 164bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) for resident companies directly or indirectly held at least 95% by another resident group company; (ii) VAT grouping election under Article 59 TVA creating a single taxable person; (iii) limited election to opt for VAT taxation on rental/immovable property operations under Article 44 TVA; and (iv) options under relevant hybrid mismatch and ATAD rules as applicable to cross-border arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) governed by Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT); if the threshold is exceeded, VAT registration becomes mandatory. Foreign businesses supplying electronic, advertising, ASO/SEO or localization services to Luxembourg taxable customers may be required to register from the first euro under the place-of-supply reverse-charge rules unless covered by the OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance system and does not require digital stamping or government API approval for B2B invoices. Mandatory B2G electronic invoicing through the PEPPOL network applies to invoices issued to public sector entities since April 2022 and to all public payments by the State from 2023. Invoices to private parties may be sent electronically provided authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility are secured through qualified electronic signatures or EDI controls; no dedicated pre-clearance filing system is imposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% applies to supplies of goods physically exported or transported by or on behalf of a taxable person to a destination outside the European Union, provided the supplier retains proper documentary evidence of departure from EU territory. For B2B services (including app store optimization, ASO, SEO, multilingual localization and advertising services) supplied to non-EU taxable customers, the place of supply is where the customer is established, so the supply is outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT or effectively zero-rated; eligibility requires evidence that the customer is an entrepreneur identified for VAT outside the EU, preferably confirmed by VAT number, contract, purchase order and payment records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank FX Payment Confirmation
Contract or Purchase Order evidencing non-EU customer VAT status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax and customs authorities may reject zero-rating claims on audit if the export substantiation bundle is incomplete or inconsistent. In such cases, unpaid VAT is reassessed together with default interest at 0.6% per month, and a fine of up to ECU/EUR 10,000 may be imposed under Article 68 of the VAT Law. Fraudulent or knowingly false export declarations trigger criminal tax fraud proceedings and civil penalties of up to double the evaded VAT, retrospective clawback of refunds, and potential criminal imprisonment. Documentation must demonstrate the economic reality of the export transaction, including actual physical departure for goods and genuine business status of non-EU customers for services.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking conduct and anti-money-laundering supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as a Eurozone member, applies full liberalisation of capital movements and current account payments under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. The euro is fully convertible without any domestic exchange-control restrictions. Capital account transactions, including equity subscriptions, shareholder loans, intercompany financing, and loan repayments, are freely permitted. Current account payments for services, royalties, and remuneration are unrestricted. Profit remittance, including dividend distributions and interest payments, is permitted after the annual accounts are approved by the shareholders and statutory audit and disclosure requirements, where applicable, have been met. A Luxembourg withholding tax applies to dividends and certain interest (normally 15% domestic rate, reduced under applicable tax treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive). There are no currency transfer taxes, no stamp duties on foreign exchange transactions, and no prior approval requirements for converting EUR to other currencies. All conversions are executed at freely negotiated market rates. Banks are subject to statistical balance-of-payments (BOP) reporting obligations to the BCL, but these reporting requirements do not restrict the timing or amount of transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, repatriation, or holding-period requirements on export proceeds. An export entity (the SARL) may freely receive and retain payments in EUR or any foreign currency in Luxembourg bank accounts or in foreign accounts without any forced conversion or time-bound remittance obligation. Only statistical reporting applies: the receiving bank must report cross-border transfers to the BCL for balance-of-payments compilation, using purpose codes and transaction classifications, without any restrictive effect on the export revenue.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Spuerkeess (Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: High for operational disbursement and collection treasury, but Low/Medium for statutory capital escrow purposes. EEA-authorized electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Payoneer Payment Europe S.à r.l. (authorised and regulated by the CSSF in Luxembourg) and Wise Europe S.A. (passporting into Luxembourg from Belgium) are fully viable for holding multicurrency working balances, settling subcontractor invoices, and managing app-marketplace payouts. However, a Luxembourg SARL’s statutory share capital must be subscribed and deposited with a licensed credit institution for the notarisation and capital verification phase; EMIs are not recognised for capital formation/deed purposes. Additional constraints: EMIs generally are non-deposit-taking entities, corporate funds held with EMIs are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme, and treasury policy should cap daily EMI balances and sweep balances to a Tier-1 credit institution. The overall rating is 'approved ancillary rail', not a replacement for main banking.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is generally expected but not formally mandatory under Luxembourg law. Most Tier-1 banks require at least one face-to-face interview with the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), the managing director, and any authorised signatories for non-resident corporate clients. Several banking groups permit remote onboarding using advanced video identification and tamper-evident e-signatures, supported by apostilled constitutional documents, a validated passport, a proof of residence, and original board resolutions. The bank’s KYC/AML team will additionally require a corporate structure diagram, source-of-funds confirmation for the initial capital deposit, and a description of the business model. In practice, for a fully remote international board, the most reliable pathway is to authorise a Luxembourg-resident corporate-services provider as a trusted introducer and to schedule a single video-call KYC review. Spuerkeess and some traditional houses may still insist on a physical branch visit for the UBO or an authorised delegate. The treasury plan should budget for at least one director trip to Luxembourg or anticipate the assisted opening route through a notary and law firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client portfolio includes natural or legal persons domiciled in FATF grey-listed jurisdictions, offshore financial centres, or countries subject to EU financial sanctions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full client KYC files (including identification, UBO certificate, signed mandates, and service/SEO/ASO agreements), the SARL’s documented risk-based due diligence policy, sanctions screening results from a reputable automated tool, transaction purpose analysis, listed invoices and issuing descriptions, a written statement demonstrating that all counterparty relationships are commercial and arm’s-length, and confirmation that no restrained-party transactions exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the registered address (notary chamber or service-provider address) and the perceived operational location due to home-office-based staff, virtual workforce, and non-resident directors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the authenticated lease or registered office agreement in Luxembourg, the bank-certified corporate authorisation, table of central administration functions performed in Luxembourg, signed employment or outsourcing contracts with freelancers/subcontractors, the entity's commercial registry excerpt (RCS), proof of CSSF/ORIAS registration of the managing agent, and a written explanation that the venture is a digital services business without a physical warehousing or office requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual or high-velocity cash flow profile: frequent inbound funding from abroad on a tight daily basis, followed by rapid outbound distribution to SEO contractors and localisation freelancers, resulting in a thin retained margin.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual audited or reviewed financial statements, detailed monthly management accounts, a board-approved transfer-pricing policy, executed agreements with each contractor, delivery confirmations and campaign reports, matching invoices between inbound agency fee revenue and outbound subcontractor payments, the company's proofs of value-added tax (VAT) treatment for B2B digital services, and a letter from the statutory auditor or independent accountant attesting to the commercial substance of the transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The standard compliant routing for a non-resident shareholder injecting equity into the Luxembourg SARL is as follows: (i) the originating bank issues a SWIFT MT103 message to the corporate EUR account at a licensed Luxembourg credit institution, referencing the unique ISIN or CUSIP if shares are represented, but more practically including the remittance reference 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION / LIBÉRATION DU CAPITAL SOCIAL'; (ii) the payment purpose code is entered as EU/ISO 20215 'EQUI' (equity-like capital contribution) or, when using the ECB/BCL statistical taxonomy, the transaction is classified as 'Direct investment – equity capital injection under the BOP list'; if the bank requires a full BOP code, the standard used by Luxembourg banks is 210 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' (as preferred by the BCL reporting system). (iii) In the case of an injection from a non-EEA shareholder, the sending bank must ensure the sender is not a shell financial institution and that the transfer is accompanied by two independent source-of-funds documents, such as a signed financial statement, an audited or notarised confirmation of the beneficial owner's capacity, a board resolution of the shareholder, and a general description of the economic rationale. (iv) The receiving bank will verify that the amount matches the authorised capital structure in the RCS, perform sanctions/AML screening, possibly block transgender if the correspondent bank does not provide full payer data, and where relevant will issue the bank certificate (attestation de dépôt) required by the notary to authenticate the capital subscription. (v) For shareholder loans instead of equity, the same MT103 rail is used, but the purpose code is 'INT' (intercompany lending) according to ISO 20022, or the BCL code for 'Direct investment – other capital / loans', and a signed shareholder loan agreement must be presented to satisfy the 'substance over form' analysis of the Luxembourg debt-equity thin-cap rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails for outbound trade disbursements (payments to subcontractors, software suppliers, media-inventory platforms, and SEO localisation specialists) are: (a) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for all beneficiaries with a Euro-area IBAN — this applies to the overwhelming majority of vendors in the EU/EEA; (b) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA beneficiaries or for currencies other than EUR; MT103 includes standard fields for value date, charges (SHAR/OUR/BEN), the ISO 20022 purpose code of the underlying commercial or service contract, and payment reference to the invoice number. (c) For repetitive monthly supplier runs, the treasury can use a single batch file constructed according to Customer-to-Bank XML (ISO 20022 pain.001), which is accepted by all Luxembourg Tier-1 banks and by Payoneer/Wise via their virtual IBAN systems. (d) Commercial letters of credit (L/Cs) under UCP 600 are not typical for intangible ASO/SEO services; a standby L/C or bank guarantee may only appear if the agency is required to pre-pay a major overseas advertising marketplace or to procure a performance bond for a significant client contract. In that isolated case, the guarantee would be issued by the Luxembourg bank at a fee and is not expected to become a recurring clearing rail. (e) All outbound disbursements must be supported by the contract, invoice, provider identification, and, where relevant, VAT/transaction documents. SEPA/SWIFT instructions must be screened against EU restrictive measures, and payments to parties in jurisdictions outside the European Economic Area require the same compliance level as the inbound flows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC forward foreign exchange contracts (FX forwards) with maturities up to 12 months, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a short-form FX confirmation
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for less-liquid currencies where no real local currency delivery is permitted onshore
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) to convert EUR receipts into USD or other foreign-currency obligations, subject to EMIR margin rules
European-style FX options (call and put) traded OTC under ISDA/CSA, used only for hedging forecast net exposures and not for speculative trading
Exchange-traded currency futures and futures options listed on Eurex or CME Globex, as liquid alternative hedging instruments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the end of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, filing deadline is 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of EUR 10 per month of delay per document; two formal notices trigger a public prosecutor petition to the local court for compulsory strike-off; maximum administrative fine up to EUR 5,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes), Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing due 30 April following the taxable period; online submission may be deferred to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties of EUR 25 to EUR 250; a 10% late-payment surcharge on the tax due and legal interest; tax enforcement proceedings may follow but not administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net Wealth Tax Return (impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes), Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing aligned with the corporate income tax return; due 30 April, online extension to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment and penalties as under CIT; a 10% surcharge and legal interest on unpaid tax, with enforced collection measures, but no direct strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of an independent réviseur d'entreprises if the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: total balance sheet assets exceed EUR 4.4 million; net turnover exceeds EUR 8.8 million; average workforce exceeds 50 employees; audit also required if the articles of association so provide or upon petition of a minority shareholder
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial accounts and annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for individual annual accounts and requested for consolidated accounts of publicly listed groups

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg has no separate annual UBO filing; the SARL must file any change of beneficial ownership with the RCS within 30 days and keep an on-site UBO register updated. The annual corporate secretary review verifies the accuracy of RCS-listed UBO data and cross-checks it against the shareholder register; administrative penalties reach EUR 1,250 for natural persons and EUR 5,000 for legal persons.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200 – US$3,400 per year (typical Luxembourg registered-office or company secretarial service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$6,000 – US$18,000 per year if mandatory audit thresholds are exceeded; otherwise not applicable

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined headline rate on taxable income above EUR 175,000, computed on the basis of the Luxembourg City municipality: 17% corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, IRC) plus 7% solidarity surcharge on the IRC (state-level effective 18.19%) plus 6.75% municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC, based on the Luxembourg City multiplier of 225% applied to the statutory base rate of 3%). The first EUR 175,000 of taxable income is taxed at 15% IRC (combined state-Communal effective rate of approximately 22.80%, again at the Luxembourg City multiplier).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Intellectual property regime under Art. 50ter LIR: 80% exemption on net qualifying IP income (qualifying assets include copyrighted software, algorithms, patents and patent-related rights, computed under the OECD nexus approach), producing a combined effective tax rate of approximately 4.99% on net qualifying IP income derived from the ASO/SEO localization technology stack. Participation exemption under Art. 166 LIR: 100% exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains on qualifying shareholdings (direct holding of at least 10% or an acquisition price of at least EUR 1,200,000, held for an uninterrupted period of at least 12 months; for dividends the participation exemption applies against fully taxable Luxembourg corporate shareholders; treaty relief or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive protects underlying foreign dividends). No withholding taxes are imposed on outbound interest or royalty payments under domestic law, benefitting cross-border intangibles licensing by the agency. The Luxembourg alternative minimum taxation is constituted mainly by the minimum net wealth tax floor, which remains applicable irrespective of IRC losses.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time limit under Art. 114 LIR); however, the annual utilisation of carried-forward losses is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the remaining taxable income in excess of that amount, and the entire carryforward is forfeited if, during any six-year period, more than 50% of the shares are directly or indirectly acquired and the company ceases to continue the same business activity.
